messages.subject: Question about inla.posterior.sample
parts:
Hello! I have a spatial binomial model and am trying to conduct bootstrap analysis using inla.posterior.sample. However, I am confused about how to move forward to get the probabilities. Here is what I have so far:

#build the mesh using x and y coordinates
mesh1 <- inla.mesh.create.helper(points=cbind(total.final.mini$x,total.final.mini$y),max.edge=c(500,2000),cutoff=0,offset=c(10,140),min.angle=c(26,21))

coords <- as.matrix(total.final.mini[,1:2])set.seed(12345)

#matern spde model object
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh1,alpha=2)

#coordinates as a matrix
coords <- as.matrix(total.final.mini[,1:2])

#Construct observation/prediction weight matrices based on mesh
A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh1,loc=coords)

#list of named index vectors for SPDE model
time.index <- inla.spde.make.index("coordinates", n.spde = spde$n.spde)

#standardize covariates
library(RegularizedSCA)

total.final.mini$neighbors.std <- (total.final.mini$neighbors - mean(total.final.mini$neighbors)) / sd(total.final.mini$neighbors)
total.final.mini$total.area.std <- (total.final.mini$total.area - mean(total.final.mini$total.area)) / sd(total.final.mini$total.area)

N <- nrow(total.final.mini)

X <- data.frame(Intercept=rep(1,N), total.final.mini$neighbors.std, total.final.mini$total.area.std)

colnames(X) <- c("Intercept","neighbors.std", "total.area.std")

#build the stack
stack3 <- inla.stack(data=list(y = total.final.mini$pres, link=1, Ntrials=1),
                     A=list(A,1),
                     effects=list(w=time.index,
                                  X=as.data.frame(X)),tag="est")

#formula
formula3 <- y ~ -1 + Intercept +
  neighbors.std + total.area.std +
  f(coordinates, model=spde)

#data object
data = inla.stack.data(stack3)

#call to inla
r3 <- inla(formula3, family="binomial",Ntrials=1,
           data=data,control.compute=list(dic=T,cpo=T,config=T), 
           control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack3),compute=TRUE,link=1,
                                  quantiles=c(0.025,0.5,0.975)))

#call inla.posterior.sample to generate one value for each of the parameters
Sim <- inla.posterior.sample(n=1,result=r3, seed=12345)

#names of my parameters
MyParams <- c("Intercept","neighbors.std","total.area.std")

#find out the row numbers for the regression parameters within the Sim object
rownum <- lapply(MyParams, function(x) grep(x,rownames(Sim[[1]]$latent),fixed=T))

rownum <- as.numeric(rownum)

#access the simulated values of the three parameters (betas) from Sim[[1]]$latent
Betas <- Sim[[1]]$latent[as.numeric(rownum)]

#we also need the simulated spatial random field (w) values. These are in:
w <- Sim[[1]]$latent[1029:2386]
head(w)

#make covariate dataframe into a matrix
Xm <- as.matrix(X)
#make A into a matrix
Am <- as.matrix(A)
dim(A)

#we can now calculate the fitted values based on the simulated parameter values
FixedPart <- Xm %*% Betas
SpatialPart <- Am %*% w

#next I want to use these simulated parameter values to simulate the response (0's and 1's) and I believe I should use rbinom, but I don't know how to get the probabilities (I assume I should do something with FixedPart and SpatialPart but not sure what.

Ysim <- rbinom(n=nrow(total.final.mini), size=1, prob=?)


Thank you!!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Question about inla.posterior.sample
parts:
On Fri, 2019-01-25 at 17:12 -0500, Carrie Perkins wrote:
>
> #we can now calculate the fitted values based on the simulated
> parameter values
> FixedPart <- Xm %*% Betas
> SpatialPart <- Am %*% w

try this

Predictor = FixedPart + SpatialPart
prob = exp(Predictor)/(1 + exp(Predictor))

Ysim <- rbinom(n=length(prob), size=1, prob=Prob)

--
Håvard Rue
Helpdesk
he...@r-inla.org
